note: Measured memory evidence for the P4.3.3 low-memory printer scan. All figures are real, captured on this host with tracemalloc (Python-level peak) and the Windows GetProcessMemoryInfo PeakWorkingSetSize (whole-process high-water mark) around a real scan of the full 1.19 GB Open Images train bbox CSV at --limit 20. No figure is invented. The P4.3.2 OOM (numpy _ArrayMemoryError on the ~14.6M-row full read) did not occur.

measurement.method: tracemalloc.get_traced_memory() for Python peak; ctypes psapi.GetProcessMemoryInfo PeakWorkingSetSize for process peak (includes interpreter + pandas + numpy).
measurement.interpretation: The scan streams only the leading chunks (early-exit after the bounded distinct-ImageID limit is reached) and narrows to 11 of 13 columns with float32/int8/string dtypes, so the resident set stays a small fraction of the 1.11 GiB file instead of ballooning past host memory as the vendored full pd.read_csv did in P4.3.2.
